headline: YOUTUBE TOOK A RECORD 15.8 PERCENT OF ALL AMERICAN TELEVISION IN A MONTH WHEN TOTAL TV VIEWING FELL 4.4 PERCENT, AND THE ONLY GROWTH NIELSEN NAMES IS A 9 PERCENT RISE AMONG THE OVER-FIFTIES
deck: Nielsen published its August Gauge yesterday and YouTube set a platform record on it.  Read the next paragraph of the release and the record gets more interesting, not less.  Everything else on television shrank, YouTube genuinely grew, and the one growth driver Nielsen puts a number on is people aged fifty and over.
tldr: YouTube took a record 15.8 percent of all American television watch time in August while total TV usage fell 4.4 percent, and the only growth Nielsen names is a 9 percent rise among adults over fifty.  Pull the age split on your last three YouTube campaigns, compare it against what the brief assumed, and commission one video made deliberately for the older viewer.

Netflix cut its own 2026 advertising target from about 3 billion dollars to about 2.7 billion and blamed slower rollout of its advertising products rather than demand, while Spotify tripled its advertising growth rate to 9 percent on auction-based buying.  Treat the selling machinery as the constraint: write a fixed-price, fixed-format rate card for whatever video inventory you control so a buyer can say yes without a meeting.

Instagram brand engagement rate per impression rose 68 percent worldwide in the third quarter while interactions per post fell from 35 to 34 and impressions per post fell 48 percent, on Emplifi's own figures.  Put absolute reach and absolute interactions in their own columns next to every rate you report, and stop sending rates on their own.

Ocean Spray says a creator trip with no required posts produced about 70 posts and more than 12 million impressions, and that last year's version beat its own polished campaign cutdowns and its own social posts.  Cost one no-obligation trip into next year's plan with zero deliverables in the invitation, and agree up front that it will be judged on posts and comments rather than impressions.

An esports tournament set a hours-watched record on 115 hours of airtime across 112 channels while holding 127,818 viewers at a typical moment, and a different tournament halved its airtime and grew its real audience 74 percent.  Ask for peak and average concurrent viewers alongside hours watched on every live property you are quoted, and divide hours by airtime yourself when a seller will not give you the average.

Two thirds of consumer brands told Forrester that bringing creative and production in-house is a high priority for the next twelve months, and Omnicom's advertising discipline shrank while its media business grew more than 10 percent.  Offer your clients fixed monthly production capacity priced against the cost of two in-house hires, rather than a campaign fee.

In Backslash's survey, 42 percent of people assume a brand engineered anything that goes viral and 33 percent suspect bots, against 25 percent who think people genuinely liked it.  Strip every view count and trending badge out of your current creative and captions, and open instead with one sentence stating a position the brand will defend.

Everything else on television shrank, YouTube genuinely grew, and the one growth driver Nielsen puts a number on is people aged fifty and over.

Treat the selling machinery as the constraint: write a fixed-price, fixed-format rate card for whatever video inventory you control so a buyer can say yes without a meeting.
